title: Quarterly portfolio map: hosted API model-catalog gap-fill & experiment slate
creator: Maya Patel
body:
Objective: produce a prioritized quarterly portfolio that balances short-term gap-fills (missing model tiers and compatibility shims) with a set of hypothesis-driven experiments to improve unit economics and quality for Hosted API customers. This ticket captures the scope, success metrics, risks, and handoffs required to finalize the roadmap slice for Q2 planning.

Context: Usage patterns in the last 8 weeks show a concentration of requests at mid-sized prompt lengths and a growing customer demand for slightly older but cheaper quantized variants. Meanwhile, inference cost per 1k tokens rose 12% month-over-month on peak days. We need a mixed plan: shore up missing endpoints (gap-fills), validate lightweight quantization experiments, and schedule a canary rotation strategy that minimizes customer disruption.

Scope: 1) Identify 6 highest-impact gap endpoints (model+config) that customers expect but we do not expose. 2) Define 3 experiments: cost-focused quantization profiles, prefix-KV cache priming for common prompts, and an adaptive routing policy (latency vs cost). 3) Map dependencies, resource owners, and an incremental rollout/canary schedule.
updates: 2026-02-10: Created ticket — initial discovery notes aggregated from console telemetry and support logs (incidents: INC-2026-021).
2026-02-12: PM sync with Applied ML — agreed on experiment hypotheses and required datasets (see link to confluence).
2026-02-15: Engineering triage — ENG owners flagged kernel selection work (ENG-4398) may add 2 sprint dependency; adjusted timeline.
2026-02-17: Design reviewed proposed API surface for exposing quantized variants; DES feedback: add explicit "compatibility" flag and migration guidance.
2026-02-20: Stakeholder readout — Sales asked for a conservative deprecation window for any endpoint impacted by routing changes; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-02-24: Finalized prioritization matrix and candidate gap-fill list; request engineering headcount for two sprints to support canary automation.
acceptance_criteria: List of 6 prioritized gap endpoints with owner and implementation notes created in Confluence (doc link in 'links').
Three experiments defined with datasets, success thresholds, and test harness (benchmarks + perf dashboards).
Canary/rollout runbook drafted with rollback triggers, monitoring dashboards, and communication templates.
Dependencies (ENG-4398, ENG-4477) scheduled and assigned; blockers documented.
Sign-off from Applied ML, Runtime Eng, and Solutions (emails archived in doc).
metrics: Primary: delta in token-unit cost (USD per 1k tokens) for target workload cohort; target -15% improvement for quantization experiment.
Secondary: 95th percentile latency change — must not exceed +10% for customers in P0 tier during canary.
Quality guardrail: no more than 2% regression in prompt-level mean ROUGE/BLEU-like evaluation sets or customer-chosen evals.
Operational: time-to-detect and rollback mean <= 15 minutes for canary incidents.
risks: Kernel/hardware compaction (ENG-4398) slips, delaying quantized variant rollout and invalidating early perf expectations.
Adaptive routing may surface edge-case regressions for region-specific customers; mitigation: region-scoped canaries and customer opt-out flag.
Customer confusion if we expose multiple similarly-named variants; mitigation: explicit naming convention + migration guide in SDKs.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize gap endpoint list and assign owners. Confluence PRD approved.
Week 1-2: Engineering implements lightweight support for 3 gap endpoints; runbench and perf baseline captured.
Week 3: Deploy quantization experiment to internal canary cohort + run automatic metrics collection (dashboard live).
Week 4: Expand canary to 10% of traffic for non-P0 customers with rollback hooks; monitor for +24h stability.
Week 5: Evaluate experiments vs acceptance criteria; if pass, schedule staged promotion and update hosted API catalog docs and SDKs.
